chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Barqi from Sa'd ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the person in ihram who shades himself from the sun. He said, 'Is it due to a valid reason (illness/defect)?' I said, 'The heat of the sun harms him while he is in ihram.' He said, 'That is a valid reason; he may shade himself and pay the ransom (fidyah).'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of ihram (sacred consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.عِلَّةٌ: A valid reason or defect justifying an exception to the general rule
key_terms.يَفْدِي: To pay the ransom (fidyah) for breaking a prohibition

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim in ihram who needs to shade themselves from the sun due to heat?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him), the concept of 'illah' (valid excuse) is applied to physical discomfort, distinguishing between mere heat and actual harm that necessitates relief. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the prohibition of shading in ihram is not absolute but conditional upon the absence of genuine hardship, allowing for the payment of fidyah as a compensatory measure. The hadith underscores the balance between ritual purity and practical ease, a key theme in the works of Shaykh al-Tusi in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*.
